explanation: This adapter targets exact interface use and executable snippet completion. Frozen-model patches indicated that the marker before an example call, the state at `def` before later attention reads, and the newline after a completed function are actionable sites. I used partial paired activation contrasts at those sites and gentler reference-style contrasts in the body, with covariance-weighted prototype readouts to limit spillover. The eight rank-2-to-8 updates were constructed analytically, statically validated, and not evaluated on an edited model.
final_message:
Built `python_reference.npz` to improve thinking-off Python function replies. Execution tests exposed three recurring failures: using a plausible but wrong function name, spending the token budget before finishing the implementation, and appending invented tests that fail when the snippet runs. On a separate 16-task check set, the unedited model passed 4 tasks as prompted, 7 with reference-solution examples, and 9 when given the exact function header.

The adapter targets the decisions behind those failures. An early edit gives user example assertions a partial function-definition cue. Middle-layer edits encourage `def` to read the supplied name and interface, while body and ending edits favor a standalone implementation over extra test code. The directions come from matched frozen-model activation contrasts. Covariance-weighted readouts use unrelated chat, other programming languages, and explicit requests for explanations or tests as preservation controls.

The file passed structural and norm checks: eight MLP down-projection updates, ranks 2–8, with a maximum update Frobenius norm of 12.7% of the corresponding base weight norm. No gradients or training were used. The reported pass counts are prompt controls, not adapter scores; the edited model was not evaluated.
